title: Tel Aviv Central Bus Station double suicide bombing
description: Two suicide bombers attacked near Tel Aviv's old central bus station on January 5, 2003, killing 23 people, including eight foreign nationals, and injuring more than 100. The al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigade claimed responsibility.

title: El Salvador Earthquake
description: An earthquake struck off El Salvador on 13 January 2001 at 17:33 UTC. USGS strong-motion documentation gives magnitude Mw 7.6. Official impact figures cited in a subsequent technical report were 944 deaths and 5,565 injuries, with more than 100,000 houses destroyed. Landslides caused extensive loss of life, including in Santa Tecla.

title: Mount Nyiragongo eruption
location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Nyiragongo erupted on January 17, 2002, sending lava through Goma and causing mass evacuation. A Smithsonian report records conflicting mortality assessments: 147 deaths reported by the UN and about 70 estimated by a subsequent medical field investigation. Both include deaths in a petrol-station explosion on January 21.

review.note: The original 100 is not established as an enumerated toll. The Smithsonian report explicitly contrasts a UN count of 147, including 60-100 petrol-station deaths, with Peter Baxter's field assessment of about 70 total and about 20 at the petrol station. This is a substantive contradiction within the same source, not resolved by attribution alone. The proposed 147 is only a documented alternative and must not be published as settled.

title: Gujarat (Bhuj) Earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Gujarat near Bhuj on 26 January 2001 at 03:16 UTC, India's Republic Day. USGS reports at least 20,000 fatalities, 166,836 injuries and nearly a million buildings damaged or destroyed.

title: Novye Aldi massacre
description: Russian OMON police conducted a house-to-house purge of the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, summarily executing at least 62 civilians. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled Russia responsible.

title: Second El Salvador Earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck the San Vicente region of El Salvador on 13 February 2001 at 14:22 UTC, one month after the January disaster. It killed 315 people and caused further destructive landslides and building collapses.

title: Daegu subway fire
description: An arson attack aboard a train at Jungangno station in Daegu spread to a second train on February 18, 2003. The fire killed 192 people and injured more than 140. Combustible interiors, smoke and failures in the evacuation response contributed to the disaster.

title: Iran Ilyushin Il-76 military plane crash
description: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards Ilyushin Il-76 flying from Zahedan to Kerman struck Mount Sirach during its approach in poor weather on February 19, 2003. All 275 occupants died. The Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives describes a premature descent below the minimum descent altitude in poor visibility.

title: Kaduna religious riots
description: Christian-Muslim violence broke out in Kaduna on 21 February 2000 during a protest against proposed Sharia legislation. A state judicial commission reported at least 1,295 deaths in the February violence. Later violence in May is excluded from that count; people interviewed by Human Rights Watch believed the total across the 2000 riots was substantially higher.

title: The Station nightclub fire
location: West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States
description: Pyrotechnics ignited polyurethane foam during a concert at The Station nightclub in West Warwick late on February 20 local time, February 21 UTC. The rapidly spreading fire killed 100 people and injured more than 200.

title: Mozambique floods and Cyclone Eline
description: Cyclone Eline worsened severe flooding already affecting Mozambique in February 2000. The wider flood and cyclone emergency killed about 700 people and affected about two million; these are cumulative emergency totals, not deaths or displacement on the landfall date alone.

title: Bogoro massacre
location: Bogoro, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: FNI and FRPI fighters attacked Bogoro in Ituri on February 24, 2003, killing at least 200 civilians. The International Criminal Court convicted Germain Katanga in connection with the attack in 2014; Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui was acquitted in 2012.

title: Al Hoceima earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Al Hoceima in northern Morocco on February 24, 2004. A subsequent regional support committee report recorded 628 deaths and 926 injuries. Thousands of homes were destroyed and more than 15,000 people displaced.

review.note: USGS gives Mw 6.4, not 6.5. ADRC preserves the March official count of 628 and 926 injured; another reference gives 631, so attribute 628 to that report rather than call it an uncontested final toll. UTC earthquake date is February 24. The later 631 figure is not reconciled with the March snapshot; changing the prose's attribution alone does not establish final mortality. Withhold pending that reconciliation.

title: Outbreak of the Darfur conflict
description: Rebel groups attacked a government air base in North Darfur, triggering a counterinsurgency campaign by the Sudanese government and allied Janjaweed militias that killed an estimated 3,000 civilians and displaced more than 600,000 people by the end of 2003. The conflict escalated into a sustained campaign of attacks on civilian villages.

review.note: HRW supports conflict beginning in February 2003, but the airfield attack belongs to April 25, not the supplied February 26 date. No checked evidence establishes precisely 3,000 civilian deaths or 600,000 displaced by December 2003. Resolve onset convention and annual scope before publication; do not present this as one day's toll.

sources.name: Human Rights and Human Welfare paper

title: SuperFerry 14 bombing
description: A bomb aboard SuperFerry 14 caused a fire near Manila Bay at about 00:50 on February 27, 2004, local time, February 26 UTC. The attack was attributed to Abu Sayyaf. The reported death toll of 116 includes missing passengers presumed dead.

title: Godhra train burning
description: A coach of the Sabarmati Express caught fire following an attack near Godhra station on 27 February 2002, killing 59 passengers, including Hindu pilgrims and activists returning from Ayodhya. The incident was followed by widespread anti-Muslim violence in Gujarat.

title: 2002 Gujarat riots
description: Weeks of communal rioting followed the Godhra train burning, with violence concentrated in Ahmedabad and other Gujarat cities. The official death toll was about 1,000, while independent estimates range up to 2,000, most of them Muslims.

review.note: HRW supports mass violence and higher estimates, but its retrospective says retaliatory attacks had already begun on 27 February, before the major 28 February escalation. The rounded official count needs a primary final tally and explicit exclusion/inclusion of Godhra victims to prevent overlap.

title: Ethiopia drought and food crisis
description: After years of failed rains, a severe drought gripped southeastern Ethiopia with 8 million facing severe food shortages. Malnutrition-related deaths ran into the low thousands before international relief averted a repeat of the 1984-85 famine.

review.note: FAO supports the regional drought and roughly eight million needing assistance. No reviewed source establishes 1 March as a discrete event or 2,000 as a measured death toll. Do not convert a broad crisis estimate into a daily count.

title: Ashura bombings in Karbala and Baghdad
description: Coordinated explosions struck Shia worshippers observing Ashura in Karbala and Baghdad on March 2, 2004. Contemporary reports gave differing casualty totals, including 182 deaths; hundreds were injured.

review.note: Contemporary RTE reports 182, while Japan's retrospective diplomatic bluebook says over 170 with over 390 injured; final 182/550 is not established. Initial weapon accounts were disputed. Correct geographic scope and remove speculative tactical detail.

title: Barakova coal mine explosion
description: An explosion at the Barakova coal mine in the Krasnodon region on March 11, 2000 killed dozens of miners. RFE/RL subsequently reported 81 deaths, while contemporary Guardian reporting gave 82.

review.note: The original 80 was an early count. RFE/RL on March 16 reports 81, while The Guardian on March 13 reports 82. The sources do not explain that reduction or establish a reconciled final count. The source-attributed 81 is a candidate correction only; the unresolved exact toll prevents publication.

title: Madrid Train Bombings
description: Bombs exploded on Madrid commuter trains during the morning rush hour on March 11, 2004. Spanish government accounts distinguish 192 victims of the train attacks from a police officer killed in the related Leganes explosion on April 3. More than 1,800 people were injured in the train bombings.

title: Chattisinghpora massacre
location: Chattisinghpora, Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir, India
description: Gunmen rounded up Sikh residents in Chattisinghpora in Anantnag district on March 20, 2000 and shot them, killing 35 people.

title: US-led invasion of Iraq
description: The US-led invasion of Iraq began on March 20, 2003, and Baghdad fell on April 9. Iraq Body Count's 2005 dossier recorded 7,299 civilian deaths during the invasion period through April 30. This is a documented period total, not deaths on the opening day or a comprehensive estimate of all war mortality.

title: Nahrin earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck the Nahrin area of Baghlan Province on 25 March 2002. Later IFRC operational reporting estimated 800 deaths and 10,000 people left homeless. Early casualty estimates were substantially higher; this figure follows the later IFRC assessment.
sources: International Charter Space and Major Disasters

title: Park Hotel Passover massacre
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked the Park Hotel in Netanya during a Passover meal on 27 March 2002, killing 30 civilians and injuring more than 100. The attack was one of the triggers for Israel's Operation Defensive Shield.

title: First Battle of Fallujah
description: US forces began an assault on Fallujah on the night of April 4, 2004, after four American contractors were killed. Iraq Body Count cites about 800 reported Iraqi deaths across the April siege and estimates that 572-616 were civilians. These cumulative figures are estimates, not a single-day count.

title: Air China Flight 129 crash
description: Air China Flight 129, a Boeing 767 flying from Beijing to Busan, struck Mount Dotdae during a circling approach to Gimhae Airport on 15 April 2002. Of 166 people aboard, 129 died and 37 survived.

title: Ryongchon train explosion
description: An ammonium-nitrate explosion at Ryongchon railway station on April 22, 2004, devastated the surrounding town. IFRC reported 161 deaths and about 1,300 injuries. The French government's accident archive records 76 children among those killed.

title: Bojaya massacre
description: On 2 May 2002, during fighting between FARC guerrillas and paramilitaries in Bellavista, Bojaya, a cylinder bomb launched by FARC struck the church where civilians had taken shelter. Colombia's victims authority later recorded at least 79 deaths and more than 100 injuries; earlier reports had put the toll at 119.

title: Riyadh compound bombings
description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers attacked three foreign residential compounds in Riyadh with car bombs, killing 35 people including nine Americans and wounding more than 160. The attacks marked the beginning of a militant campaign inside Saudi Arabia.

review.note: Rewards for Justice explicitly reports 35 killed, including nine Americans, but another US government chronology reports 34 including nine attackers. Their fatality populations do not clearly align. Date, three compounds and al-Qaeda attribution are supported; victim-only versus attacker-inclusive scope needs resolution before accepting 35.

title: Znamenskoye truck bombing
description: A suicide truck bombing struck a government and security compound in Znamenskoye, Chechnya, on May 12, 2003. A UN chronology records 59 people killed. The attack also injured about 200 people.

review.note: UN chronology supports May 12 and 59 deaths. Checked sources do not establish the claim that Basayev claimed responsibility. Remove that assertion rather than converting allegations into fact; exact attacker inclusion is not specified in the UN total. That unresolved attacker/victim scope remains a publication blocker despite the supported shorter prose.

title: Enschede fireworks disaster
description: A fire at a fireworks depot escalated into massive explosions, killing 23 people including four firefighters. The blasts destroyed around 400 homes.

title: Casablanca bombings
description: Coordinated suicide bombings struck several sites in Casablanca on May 16, 2003, including a Spanish restaurant and Jewish-associated targets. The reported total of 45 deaths includes 33 victims and 12 bombers; about 100 people were injured.

title: Boumerdès earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck offshore near Zemmouri in Boumerdes Province on May 21, 2003, causing extensive destruction in northern Algeria. Algeria's CRAAG reports 2,365 deaths, while other summaries give 2,266; the totals are not reconciled here.

review.note: Full CRAAG text confirms May 21 at 19:44 local time and Mw 6.8, but reports 2,365 deaths, not the original/reference-summary figure of 2,266. The earlier ledger note missed this contradiction. No source-level reconciliation establishes a final total. Remove the ranking, injury and homelessness precision, and withhold the row pending mortality reconciliation.

title: Poso sectarian riots
description: The third and deadliest phase of the Poso riots between Christian and Muslim communities. An estimated 300 people were killed.

review.note: HRW identifies May-June 2000 as the third phase and explains that aggregate fatality counts are uncertain. Exact 23 May onset and phase-specific 300 deaths were not established by the reviewed evidence.

title: China Airlines Flight 611 disaster
description: China Airlines Flight 611, a Boeing 747 traveling from Taipei to Hong Kong, broke up in mid-air about 20 minutes after takeoff and crashed into the Taiwan Strait. All 225 passengers and crew were killed.

title: Dolphinarium Discotheque Bombing
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked outside the Dolphinarium discotheque in Tel Aviv on June 1, 2001, killing 21 other people, most of them teenagers, and injuring at least 120.

title: Nepalese Royal Palace Massacre
description: A shooting at Narayanhity Royal Palace in Kathmandu on 1 June 2001 ultimately left ten members of Nepal's royal family dead, including King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and Crown Prince Dipendra. An official inquiry attributed the killings of nine relatives to Dipendra, who died on 4 June. Gyanendra succeeded him as king.

title: Southern Africa food crisis
description: Southern Africa faced a regional food and health emergency in 2002. WHO warned in August that the crisis could cause 300,000 additional deaths over the following six months; that was a projection, not a measured death toll. WFP later reported that relief helped prevent the food crisis from becoming a famine.

review.note: Critical: 300,000 was WHO's prospective warning of possible additional deaths, not observed mortality. Statements were issued in August/October, not 1 June. No defensible positive replacement toll or daily date established. Quarantine/remove from observed-death totals pending resolution; do not retain the projection as actual deaths.

title: Jerusalem bus 32A bombing
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked Egged bus 32A near Patt Junction in Jerusalem during the morning rush hour on 18 June 2002, killing 19 other people and wounding more than 70.

title: Afghanistan Drought and Famine Crisis
description: Afghanistan's third consecutive year of severe drought brought the country to the brink of famine, with FAO and WFP reporting that about 5.5 million people faced severe food shortages by mid-2001. World Bank and UN officials warned of famine conditions and reported thousands of deaths from starvation and exposure, though the total death toll was never precisely counted.

review.note: FAO/WFP confirms a third drought year and famine risk. The 5.5 million assistance target is documented in September, not a specific 21 June incident. Neither a 5,000 death toll nor the asserted World Bank attribution is established.

title: Bou'in-Zahra earthquake
description: An earthquake struck the Avaj and Changureh area of northwestern Iran on June 22, 2002 at 02:58 UTC, severely damaging villages in Qazvin and neighboring regions. A disaster-science field report recorded about 261 deaths.
sources: Japan Society for Natural Disaster Science

title: Southern Peru Earthquake
description: A magnitude 8.4 earthquake struck off the coast of southern Peru, killing roughly 100 people and injuring more than 1,300, with most deaths in the Arequipa region. The quake triggered a tsunami that killed about two dozen people in the Camaná area and damaged or destroyed thousands of buildings, including historic structures in Arequipa.

review.note: USGS confirms 23 June, Mw 8.4, southern Peru and tsunami. EERI's initial assessment gives 77 dead, 68 missing and 2,713 wounded; the record mixes rounded and preliminary figures. Final deaths versus missing and tsunami subtotal require reconciliation before changing 100.

title: Uberlingen mid-air collision
description: A Bashkirian Airlines Tupolev Tu-154 carrying 69 people, including many children en route to a Spanish holiday, collided with a DHL cargo Boeing 757 over southern Germany. All 71 people on both aircraft died.
sources: German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation

title: Yangtze and Huaihe river floods
description: Seasonal floods along the Huaihe and Yangtze river basins in central and eastern China inundated large areas of Anhui, Jiangsu, and Henan provinces during the summer, killing about 1,551 people and affecting more than 100 million. It was the worst flooding in China since the 1998 Yangtze floods.

review.note: 1,551 is the nationwide annual flood total across 30 provincial-level areas, not an established Huaihe/Yangtze event toll. MFA reported 676 nationwide by July 20. July 1 onset and the Anhui-only location are unsupported for this aggregate. Must choose an event-specific scope and date before replacing the count.

title: Typhoon Utor (Feria)
description: Utor, known as Feria in the Philippines, passed northern Luzon on 4 July 2001 and caused destructive flooding and landslides. A subsequent monthly storm summary reported at least 168 deaths in the Philippines. The storm then struck southern China, where additional deaths occurred; those are not included in this Philippine toll.

title: Sudan Airways Flight 139 crash
description: Sudan Airways Flight 139, a Boeing 737, crashed near Port Sudan on July 8, 2003, killing 116 of its 117 occupants. After an engine failed following takeoff, the crew returned toward the airport; the aircraft struck terrain on approach in limited visibility.

title: Second siege of Monrovia
description: LURD rebels besieged the Liberian capital Monrovia from June to August 2003, shelling civilian neighborhoods, churches, and schools and killing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 civilians. The siege ended when President Charles Taylor went into exile and international peacekeepers arrived.
sources: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights

review.note: Sources describe several June-July offensives and a July 18-August siege, not a clearly named second siege with a 1,500 final civilian toll. HRW documents hundreds killed and over 2,000 injured, while the summary gives 1,000 killed. Dates, episode naming and civilian estimate need reconciliation.

title: Colombo Airport Attack
description: LTTE suicide commandos attacked Bandaranaike International Airport and the adjoining air force base near Colombo, killing at least 18 people and destroying or damaging 11-13 aircraft, including several SriLankan Airlines jets. The attack caused an estimated $350 million in losses to the national carrier alone.

review.note: Early reporting gave at least 18 including attackers; later accounts give seven servicemen and 14 attackers. The original does not define its scope and aircraft-loss figures vary. The documented 03:50 local start on 24 July is 23 July UTC (Sri Lanka then UTC+6). Proposed date/location only; resolve toll and damage claims before integration.

title: Sknyliv air show disaster
description: A Ukrainian Air Force Su-27 crashed into spectators during an aerobatic display at Sknyliv airfield near Lviv on 27 July 2002. The disaster killed 77 people, including 28 children, and injured hundreds.

title: Darfur genocide (2004 killings)
description: The armed conflict in Darfur, in which the Sudanese government and allied Janjaweed militias systematically attacked civilian villages, killed tens of thousands of people and displaced more than a million during 2004. United Nations and WHO estimates of deaths in 2004 ranged from about 30,000 to 71,000, mostly from violence, starvation and disease.

review.note: 70,000 was WHO's estimated mortality among displaced people from living conditions in accessible Darfur areas during March-mid-October 2004, excluding violent deaths. It is neither all 2004 killings nor a July 30 event. Need a defensible interval, title and mortality scope; avoid overlap with the 2003 onset record.

title: European heat wave
description: Extreme heat affected Europe during summer 2003, with a major peak in August. A retrospective study estimated more than 70,000 excess deaths over the summer, including deaths before August; this is a seasonal excess-mortality estimate rather than a single-day toll.
sources: French Institute for Public Health Surveillance (InVS)

review.note: Peer-reviewed estimate concerns excess mortality over summer 2003; more than 20,000 excess deaths preceded August. August 1 cannot anchor the whole mortality interval without an explicit convention. The air-conditioning/majority claim is unsupported and removed; toll is an estimate, not certified heat deaths.

sources.name: Robine et al., UKHSA research portal
Robine et al., full paper via WMO

title: Pushkin Square bombing
description: A bomb exploded in a pedestrian underpass near Moscow's Pushkin Square during the evening rush hour on 8 August 2000. Officials investigated several possible motives; no group claimed responsibility at the time.

review.note: Contemporary reporting supports date, rush-hour underpass attack and explicitly uncertain responsibility. It gives preliminary deaths, not the later 13. Remove definitive Chechen linkage; final toll still needs a reliable later source.

title: Sbarro Pizzeria Bombing
description: A suicide bombing at the Sbarro pizzeria in Jerusalem on 9 August 2001 killed 15 civilians initially and wounded about 130. Chana Nachenberg died in May 2023 after remaining unconscious since the attack, bringing the victim toll to 16, excluding the bomber.

title: Typhoon Rananim
description: Typhoon Rananim made landfall in Zhejiang on August 12, 2004, causing destructive winds, floods and landslides. Xinhua's August 16 tally reported 164 deaths and 24 missing in Zhejiang; later summaries give a higher death count.

review.note: 164 dead and 24 missing was the August 16 snapshot, also used by HKO, while later summaries give 168 in China. The 1956 comparison applies to Zhejiang, not all mainland China. Date of landfall is established, but final toll needs reconciliation.

title: Central European floods
description: Days of record rainfall in August 2002 caused catastrophic flooding along the Elbe, Danube and Vltava rivers, inundating Dresden, Prague and other cities. About 110 people died across central Europe and Russia, with damages exceeding $15 billion.

review.note: This is a multi-country, multi-day disaster. 13 August is a reporting/peak date rather than established onset. Sources differ on whether Russian floods are included; the stated location omits Russia despite including it in the toll. No consistent 110-death geographic/time scope or $15bn basis established.

title: Canal Hotel (UN Baghdad headquarters) bombing
description: A suicide truck bombing struck the Canal Hotel, the UN headquarters in Baghdad, on August 19, 2003. It killed 22 people, including UN special representative Sergio Vieira de Mello and other UN staff.

title: Typhoon Bilis
description: Typhoon Bilis made landfall in southern Taiwan on August 22, 2000 before crossing toward mainland China. NOAA reports winds of about 258 km/h and more than 70 deaths across Taiwan and mainland China.

review.note: NOAA supports 22 August landfall, winds over 200 km/h and over 70 deaths in Taiwan and mainland China; CWA supports the date. Remove unqualified all-time Taiwan intensity record, which depends on measurement and comparison. Exact 71 is not established by the reviewed over-70 source; withhold pending exact mortality evidence.

title: Russian passenger plane bombings
description: Two passenger aircraft departing Moscow were destroyed by suicide bombings over Tula and Rostov oblasts on August 24, 2004. Russia's report to ICAO counted all 90 occupants, including the attackers, as killed. Investigators identified explosive devices detonated in flight.

title: Mumbai twin bomb blasts
description: Twin car bombs exploded at the Gateway of India and the Zaveri Bazaar jewellery market during the lunch hour, killing 52 people and injuring more than 200. Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba was suspected, and three people were later convicted for the attack.

review.note: Later court reporting disagrees: 54 in New Indian Express versus 52 in AFP/Dawn; even the reference summary conflicts internally. Date, targets and three convictions are corroborated, but the final incident-only toll needs a court or police source distinguishing other blasts in the prosecution.

title: Imam Ali Mosque bombing in Najaf
description: A bombing outside the Imam Ali shrine in Najaf on August 29, 2003, killed Ayatollah Mohammed Baqir al-Hakim and many other worshippers. Iraq Body Count records a range of 83-126 deaths; contemporary reporting gave differing totals.

review.note: 95 includes al-Hakim, not 95 plus him. PBS updated contemporary count to 95 with 142 wounded; IBC retains 83-126 deaths. Exact final count and over-200 injury claim remain unsettled. Proposed prose preserves the range instead of pretending a final total is established.

title: Typhoon Rusa
description: Typhoon Rusa, the strongest typhoon to strike South Korea in more than four decades, made landfall near Goheung on August 31, 2002. It killed 238 people across South Korea, Japan and North Korea and caused about $4.2 billion in damage.

review.note: JTWC confirms 31 August Goheung landfall. Korean retrospective reports 246 dead or missing in South Korea; that is not interchangeable with 238 confirmed deaths across three countries. Need country-specific dead/missing reconciliation and intensity-superlative definition.

title: Rizhskaya metro station bombing
description: A female suicide bomber detonated an explosive device near the Rizhskaya metro station in Moscow, killing 10 people and wounding more than 50. The attack, linked to Chechen separatist militants, came one week after the bombing of two Russian passenger planes.

review.note: Contemporary reports give ten total deaths; later accounts differ on whether that includes the bomber and accomplice. Russian reference explicitly includes both, while AP wording suggests a larger victim-only count. Date and location established; do not silently equate totals with innocent victims.

title: Beslan school siege
description: Militants seized School Number One in Beslan on September 1, 2004, holding more than 1,100 people hostage. Explosions and an armed assault ended the siege on September 3. The civilian death toll was 334, including 186 children; attackers also died.
sources: European Court of Human Rights case-law note

title: Assassination of Ahmad Shah Massoud
description: Two al-Qaeda operatives posing as journalists detonated a bomb hidden in a camera while interviewing Ahmad Shah Massoud, the military leader of the Afghan Northern Alliance, killing him and one other person. The assassination came two days before the September 11 attacks and removed the alliance's most effective commander ahead of the US invasion.

review.note: UNAMA supports the 9 September assassination by attackers posing as journalists. The second non-attacker death and camera-versus-battery concealment require stronger direct evidence; 'most effective commander' is an assessment, not an established factual rank.

title: Mekong Delta floods
description: The worst flooding in the Mekong Delta in decades inundated more than 825,000 homes and affected over 5 million people. 482 people died, most of them children.

review.note: ADRC supports major prolonged flooding and 825,000 inundated homes, but not a discrete 10 September event or final 482 toll. Mekong Commission's later table gives a different national total (453). Geographic and reporting-period reconciliation is required.

title: September 11 Attacks
location: New York City, Arlington, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, United States
description: Al-Qaeda hijackers flew commercial airliners into the World Trade Center towers and the Pentagon. A fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back. 2,977 people were killed.

title: Jakarta Stock Exchange bombing
description: A car bomb exploded in the underground car park of the Jakarta Stock Exchange on 13 September 2000, killing 15 people. Four men were subsequently convicted in connection with the attack, including two soldiers sentenced to life imprisonment in August 2001.

title: Bangladesh floods
description: Severe flooding affected western and southwestern Bangladesh in September 2000, forcing large numbers of residents from their homes. The IFRC described major inundation in border districts on 22 September. Contemporary casualty and displacement figures were provisional.

review.note: The description incorrectly says two million drowned: sources describe homelessness or affected population. IFRC dates the major western-border inundation to 22 September; 15 September and 150 deaths are not established. Published counts differ by event scope, so no replacement date or toll is asserted.

title: 2001 Anthrax Attacks
description: Anthrax-contaminated letters, including mail postmarked 18 September 2001, caused 22 infections and five deaths in the United States. CDC estimated that 32,000 people began preventive antibiotics. The FBI closed its investigation in 2010 after concluding Bruce Ivins was responsible. A National Research Council review found the scientific evidence linking the letter material to a particular laboratory flask less conclusive than the Justice Department had stated.

title: Hurricane Jeanne flooding in Haiti
description: Torrential rains from Tropical Storm Jeanne triggered catastrophic flash flooding and mudslides in Haiti, most severely in the coastal city of Gonaives, which was left largely submerged. The Haitian government's final tally recorded 3,006 deaths, including 2,826 in Gonaives, with about 200,000 people affected.

review.note: NOAA confirms catastrophic Haiti flooding and over 3,000 deaths, but exact 3,006/2,826 and the asserted final-government provenance were not established from accessible primary text. NHC report fetch was blocked; archive search found it but not its casualty discussion. September 18 is an onset label for flooding extending into September 19.

title: MV Le Joola capsizing
description: The overloaded Senegalese ferry Le Joola capsized off The Gambia late on 26 September 2002 while traveling from Ziguinchor to Dakar. The official toll was 1,863 dead or presumed dead, and 64 people survived.

title: Start of the Second Intifada
description: The Second Intifada began after Israeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visited the Temple Mount compound. By end of 2000, roughly 300 people had been killed.

review.note: Sharon's visit and the late-September onset are supported, but 300 by year-end is not established by the cited December report, which ends 2 December and separates populations. Need a defined inclusive date range and victim scope; the count is not a 28 September toll.

title: Srinagar Legislative Assembly Attack
description: A vehicle bombing and armed attack struck the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly complex in Srinagar on October 1, 2001. India's Home Ministry subsequently attributed the attack to Jaish-e-Mohammed and recorded 38 deaths. Published casualty breakdowns disagree on whether attackers are included.

review.note: Further research establishes October 1 and the attack identity in an MHA gazette notification, which gives 38 deaths. However, SATP's 2001 assessment includes four attackers within 38, while its 2000-2017 table lists 38 victims plus three attackers (41 total); its timeline also contains 36. These are material scope conflicts, not merely unsupported injury/occupancy prose. Remove the original 60-injured and no-legislators claims, but do not certify a victim-only total.

sources.name: South Asia Terrorism Portal: attack table

title: Beltway sniper attacks
location: Washington metropolitan area, Maryland and Virginia, United States
description: John Allen Muhammad and Lee Boyd Malvo carried out shootings across the Washington metropolitan area in October 2002. Beginning on 2 October, the regional series killed ten people and critically injured three before the suspects were captured on 24 October.

title: US-Led Invasion of Afghanistan
description: The US-led air campaign in Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001. The Project on Defense Alternatives estimated that 1,000-1,300 civilians were killed directly by bombing between that date and 1 January 2002. The recorded figure is the lower end of that estimate for the campaign period, not a count for 7 October alone.

title: USS Cole bombing
description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers rammed an explosive-laden boat into the USS Cole as it refuelled. Seventeen American sailors were killed and 39 wounded.
sources: US Naval History and Heritage Command

title: Bali bombings
description: Three bombs exploded in Kuta and Denpasar on Bali, including a large car bomb outside the Sari Club nightclub, in an attack linked to Jemaah Islamiyah. The bombings killed 202 people, mostly foreign tourists, and injured more than 200.

title: Daping coal mine gas explosion
description: A gas explosion at the Daping coal mine near Xinmi in Henan Province on October 20, 2004, killed 148 miners.

title: Typhoon Tokage
description: Typhoon Tokage crossed Japan on October 20, 2004, bringing destructive rain, floods and landslides. Official records list 95 deaths and three missing. It was the tenth typhoon to make landfall in Japan that year.
sources: Japan Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism

title: Moscow theater siege (Nord-Ost)
description: Chechen militants seized the Dubrovka theater in Moscow on October 23, taking more than 900 hostages. Russian security forces pumped an incapacitating gas into the building on October 26; at least 130 hostages died, most of them from the gas.

review.note: Dates, more than 900 hostages and gas-related deaths are supported. ECHR case material and HRW record 129 while later summaries give 130 or higher; final official 130 and the claimed lower-bound wording need reconciliation, not averaging.

title: Niigata Chuetsu earthquake
description: The October 23, 2004, Niigata Chuetsu earthquake and subsequent activity caused 68 deaths and 4,805 injuries. JMA gives magnitude 6.8 on its scale. Some 3,175 homes were destroyed and peak evacuation exceeded 100,000 people.

title: Second Battle of Fallujah
description: US-led forces launched an offensive against insurgents in Fallujah in November 2004. Civilian and combatant death estimates vary, and available civilian counts cover different areas and periods. Iraq Body Count records 581-670 civilian deaths in nine neighborhoods.
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross

review.note: Numeric 1,000 is not a defensible overall count when the prose itself gives larger combatant losses before civilians. IBC's 581-670 covers nine neighborhoods, not a complete battle census; the reported 800 was an anonymous unofficial Red Cross estimate, not a verified ICRC institutional total. Need consistent full-battle population and interval.

title: Podi Coal Mine Explosion
description: A gas explosion at the Podi coal mine in Jiaocheng County, Shanxi, on November 15, 2001 killed 33 people. A subsequent investigation found that ventilation failures allowed gas to accumulate and that the mine had resumed production without the required authorization.

title: Istanbul bombings
description: Truck bombings targeted two Istanbul synagogues on November 15, 2003, and the British consulate and HSBC offices on November 20. The attacks were linked to al-Qaeda. Reported death totals vary, including whether the four bombers are counted.

review.note: Two attack dates are established, but later totals differ: BBC summary 58; detailed reference 59 including four bombers; original 57 not reconciled. Remove the unqualified all-time Turkish superlative. Count covers both November 15 and 20, not only the indexed date.

title: Qala-i-Jangi Fortress Uprising
description: Taliban and al-Qaeda prisoners revolted at the Qala-i-Jangi fortress near Mazar-i-Sharif, triggering a six-day battle in which up to 400 prisoners, about 73 Northern Alliance fighters, and CIA officer Johnny Spann — the first American killed in combat in the war — died. Only 86 of the more than 400 prisoners survived, including American Taliban fighter John Walker Lindh.

review.note: 400 was an upper-end prisoner estimate, not a verified total including Northern Alliance and US deaths. Accounts differ on duration and fighter losses; 86 survivors is reported. A single precise aggregate cannot be inferred from these incompatible estimates.

title: Chenjiashan coal mine gas explosion
description: A gas explosion at Chenjiashan coal mine near Tongchuan, Shaanxi, killed 166 miners. It occurred at about 07:10 on November 28, 2004, local time, November 27 UTC. Fire and toxic gases hampered rescue and recovery.

title: Philippines typhoon series and Quezon floods
description: Several tropical cyclones caused severe flooding and landslides in the Philippines in November and early December 2004. A December WHO report recorded 1,060 deaths and 559 missing. Winnie caused much of the destruction, including in Quezon Province.

review.note: WHO release reproduced by ScienceDaily gives 1,060 dead and 559 missing, not 566, as a December snapshot. NASA establishes several storms over November-December and Winnie on November 29. November 30 is not a substantiated onset for the series, and Quezon alone does not describe its total scope.

title: Ben Yehuda Street Bombings
description: Two suicide bombers struck the Ben Yehuda pedestrian area in Jerusalem on 1 December 2001, followed by a car bomb. Eleven people were killed and more than 130 injured. Hamas claimed responsibility.

title: Haifa Bus 16 Bombing
description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked bus 16 in Haifa on 2 December 2001, killing 15 other people and wounding about 40. The attack followed the previous night's bombings in Jerusalem.

title: Indian Parliament Attack
description: Five gunmen attacked India's Parliament complex in New Delhi on 13 December 2001. Eight security personnel and a gardener were killed, and all five attackers were shot dead. Indian authorities attributed the attack to Pakistan-based militant groups.

title: Luoyang Dongdu commercial building fire
description: A fire caused by welding work spread through the Dongdu commercial building in Luoyang on 25 December 2000, killing 309 people. Smoke reached a crowded dance hall; investigators said the welders left without raising the alarm.
sources: French Ministry of Ecological Transition, ARIA

title: Bam earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck Bam and surrounding communities in southeastern Iran on December 26, 2003. It destroyed much of the city and killed tens of thousands. Published fatality totals differ; the World Bank's reconstruction report used approximately 26,000.

review.note: Magnitude 6.6 and December 26 UTC are supported. Fatality accounts conflict: World Bank about 26,000, Iranica 31,824-43,000, and the reference summary cites later 34,000 versus an earlier revised 26,271. Do not silently treat one precise figure as settled. The 1990 Iranian quake also makes 'deadliest in decades' unsafe.

title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
description: The December 26, 2004, earthquake off northern Sumatra generated a devastating Indian Ocean tsunami. NOAA and UNESCO's 2024 summary records 227,899 people killed or missing and presumed dead in 15 countries, with about 1.7 million displaced.

title: Grozny government headquarters bombing
description: Suicide attackers drove explosive-laden vehicles into the Chechen government headquarters in Grozny on 27 December 2002. The reported victim toll was 83, excluding the attackers.

title: Rizal Day bombings
description: Coordinated bombings struck five locations across Metro Manila on a national holiday, killing 22 people. The deadliest blast hit a crowded LRT train.
